content.text:
I submitted index 3 (Ni 0.20 / V 0.80). It gave the highest photocurrent of the three compositions I measured, 7.27 µA.

All three merit measurements are used:

| Index | Ni fraction | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 14 | 0.65 | 0.07 µA |
| 7 | 0.29 | 1.14 µA |
| 3 | 0.20 | 7.27 µA |

Photocurrent climbs sharply as the film gets more vanadium-rich. That means the more V-rich candidates I didn't measure, index 11 (Ni 0.16) and index 13 (Ni 0.13), could be better than index 3. I have no measurement to show it either way. The Gaussian-process model also ranked index 3 as the best next pick before I measured it.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements, so which crystal phase is behind the high photocurrent is unconfirmed. From the known phases, that composition would sit near Ni₂V₈O₁₅ or a mix of NiV₂O₆ and V₂O₅.
